The continuum first-mode integral factors as sin(u)(1−cos u)(3cos²u−cos u−1)/3, with a simple interior zero on [20π/91,2π/9]. The displayed trigonometric formulas give uniformly positive integrals for modes 2–6 (in particular cos²(2π/9)>7/12 for mode 2); bounding the two sum frequencies ℓ±3 gives the positive continuum margin for ℓ≥7. For finite modes, Abel summation gives a bound N/ℓ on the weighted cosine term for ℓ≤N/2, whereas the unmodulated weight sum is >2m/5 uniformly for large m. This controls ℓ≥32, with fixed-mode uniform Riemann convergence controlling 2–31. The cos-sum identity gives the centered variable M=m+1/2 exactly; the cosecant expansion in C¹ gives G_m(n)/n=J(t)+t²E(t)/M²+O(M^−4), t=M/n, with uniform J'<0 near the limiting interval and opposite endpoint signs. Inversion gives the unique real zero κM+(E/J')/M+O(M^−3), where reduction by 3c²−c−1=0 recovers the stated negative A. Strict stability signs give nonlinear quotient attraction or instability for integer networks; nothing is inferred at equality or outside the interval. Independent geometric-sum bisection at m=100,236,536 gives M³-scaled residuals about −0.3811, −0.3811, −0.3804, with positive noncritical spectral margins at the neighboring integers.
